chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Dates are superior in the Fitra (Zakat al-Fitr) compared to other foods, because they provide benefit more quickly; and that is because when it falls into the hand of its owner, he eats from it.
He said, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Zakat was revealed while the people did not yet have wealth, so it was the Fitra (Zakat al-Fitr).'.

key_terms.الْفِطْرَةِ: Fitra (Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: Why are dates preferred for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the practical wisdom of selecting dates for Zakat al-Fitr due to their rapid consumption and immediate nutritional benefit, while also linking the obligation to the historical context of early Muslim society where cash wealth was scarce. This narration underscores the flexibility of the Fitra as a food-based charity, reflecting the socio-economic realities of the time when the revelation occurred. The emphasis on dates aligns with the Prophetic tradition of breaking fasts with them, reinforcing their spiritual and physical significance in Islamic practice.
